steps.label: Separable con sustantivo
steps.sentence: She **turned off** the TV. / She **turned** the TV **off**.

steps.label: Separable con pronombre
steps.sentence: She **turned it off**.
steps.change: Con pronombre, la partícula va después: nunca “turned off it”.

steps.label: Inseparable
steps.sentence: She **looks after** the kids. → She **looks after** them.
steps.change: No se separa: nunca “looks them after”.

steps.label: De tres partes
steps.sentence: I can’t **put up with** him.

C1-1-0.title: Registro: phrasal verb vs. verbo formal

items.example: I can’t put up with the noise.
The policy does not tolerate abuse.

items.a: I stopped smoking.
items.b: I stopped to smoke.
items.note: La primera: dejé el cigarrillo. La segunda: me detuve para fumar.

items.a: Remember to text me.
items.b: I remember texting you.
items.note: “Remember to” = no olvides hacerlo; “remember + -ing” = tengo el recuerdo.

items.a: Try to open the window.
items.b: Try opening the window.
items.note: “Try to” = haz el esfuerzo; “try + -ing” = pruébalo como solución.

items.a: I regret to tell you…
items.b: I regret telling you…
items.note: “Regret to” anuncia una mala noticia; “regret + -ing” = me arrepiento de haberlo hecho.

items.a: He went on talking.
items.b: He went on to talk about prices.
items.note: “Go on + -ing” = siguió; “go on to” = pasó a otro tema.

branches.if: enjoy, avoid, mind, suggest, deny, risk
branches.example: She denied taking the money.

branches.if: decide, hope, offer, refuse, promise, afford
branches.example: We can’t afford to wait.

branches.if: una preposición (in, at, of, instead of)
branches.example: Instead of calling, she wrote.

branches.if: stop, remember, try, regret, go on
branches.example: I’ll never forget meeting her.

steps.label: Deber futuro
steps.sentence: **Remember to lock** the door.
steps.change: Algo que todavía hay que hacer.

steps.label: Recuerdo pasado
steps.sentence: I **remember locking** the door.
steps.change: La acción ocurrió antes del recuerdo.

steps.label: Negativo
steps.sentence: I **don’t remember locking** it.

steps.label: Olvido
steps.sentence: I **forgot to lock** it.

branches.if: want, expect, tell, ask, advise, allow, get
branches.example: I want you to try this on.
They made us wait outside.
I saw her leave the building.

branches.if: see, hear, watch, notice (acción en progreso)
branches.example: I saw her leaving the building.

steps.label: Activa con make
steps.sentence: They **made him wait**.

steps.label: Pasiva con make
steps.sentence: He **was made to wait**.

steps.label: Activa con let
steps.sentence: They **let us leave** early.

steps.label: Sin pasiva de let
steps.sentence: We **were allowed to leave** early.
steps.change: “Let” no tiene pasiva: usa “be allowed to”.

items.a: I want you to come.
items.b: I want that you come.
items.note: En inglés no se usa “that” + subjuntivo con “want”.

items.a: She made me laugh.
items.b: She made me to laugh.
items.note: Después de “make” + objeto, verbo sin “to”.

items.a: I heard him sing.
items.b: I heard him singing.
items.note: La primera: oí toda la canción. La segunda: lo oí mientras cantaba.

C1-2-1.title: Pon el foco en la idea clave

steps.label: Frase neutral
steps.sentence: Her confidence impresses me.

steps.label: Hendida con what
steps.sentence: **What impresses me is** her confidence.

steps.label: Destacar una acción
steps.sentence: **What she did was** change the whole design.
steps.change: Para una acción: What + sujeto + did + was (to) + verbo.

steps.label: Hendida con it
steps.sentence: **It was** her confidence **that** impressed me.

branches.example: What I need is a holiday.
What we did was call the police.
It was in Medellín that we met.
All I want is some peace and quiet.

items.a: What I need is a new suit.
items.b: What I need are new shoes.
items.note: “Be” suele concordar con lo que viene después.

items.a: What she did was change the plan.
items.b: What she did was she changed the plan.
items.note: Después de “What … did was” va el verbo base (o to + verbo), sin repetir el sujeto.

items.a: What I love is the colour.
items.b: That I love is the colour.
items.note: En español “lo que” = “what”, nunca “that”.

C1-3-0.title: ¿A/an, the o nada?
C1-3-0.question: ¿Cómo es el sustantivo en tu frase?

branches.if: Singular contable, se menciona por primera vez o es uno de muchos
branches.example: A breakthrough was announced today.
The breakthrough we discussed is real. / the internet
It’s the first trial of its kind.

branches.if: Idea general en plural o incontable
branches.example: Technology changes fast. Robots are cheaper now.

branches.if: Institución con su función general (school, hospital, university)
branches.example: She’s at university. He’s in hospital.

steps.label: Primera mención
steps.sentence: **A** team has developed **a** new test.

steps.label: Segunda mención
steps.sentence: **The** test costs less than a dollar.

steps.label: Generalización
steps.sentence: **Tests** like this save lives.

steps.label: Idea abstracta
steps.sentence: **Science** moves faster than **bureaucracy**.

items.a: Technology changes fast.
items.b: The technology changes fast.
items.note: En general, sin artículo; con “the” hablarías de una tecnología específica.

items.a: She’s in hospital.
items.b: She’s in the hospital.
items.note: UK: “in hospital” = internada; “the hospital” = el edificio (US usa “the” en ambos casos).

items.a: an hour / a university
items.b: a hour / an university
items.note: “A / an” depende del sonido, no de la letra.

steps.label: Razón
steps.sentence: **Because she felt curious**, she opened the app.

steps.label: Cláusula -ing
steps.sentence: **Feeling curious**, she opened the app.

steps.label: Acción anterior
steps.sentence: **After they had tested** the device, they published the results.

steps.label: Perfecta
steps.sentence: **Having tested** the device, they published the results.

steps.label: Negativa
steps.sentence: **Not knowing** the password, he gave up.

C1-3-1.title: ¿Qué forma de -ing clause?
C1-3-1.question: ¿Qué relación hay con la acción principal?

branches.if: Ocurre al mismo tiempo o da la razón
branches.example: Feeling tired, I went to bed.

branches.if: Ocurre antes que la acción principal
branches.example: Having finished the report, she left.
Not wanting to wait, we took a taxi.
Shocked by the news, he sat down.

items.a: Feeling curious, she opened the app.
items.b: Feeling curious, the app was opened.
items.note: En la segunda, parece que la app sentía curiosidad.

items.a: Walking home, I saw an accident.
items.b: Walking home, an accident happened.
items.note: El sujeto de la cláusula principal debe ser quien camina.

items.a: Not knowing the answer, he stayed quiet.
items.b: Knowing not the answer, he stayed quiet.
items.note: La negación va antes del -ing.

steps.label: Directo
steps.sentence: “I **will** come **tomorrow**,” he said.

steps.label: Indirecto
steps.sentence: He said (that) he **would** come **the next day**.
steps.change: will → would; tomorrow → the next day.

steps.label: Directo
steps.sentence: “I **broke** the mirror **here**,” she admitted.

steps.label: Indirecto
steps.sentence: She admitted (that) she **had broken** the mirror **there**.

C1-4-0.title: Qué tan fiable suena la afirmación

items.example: He claimed the house was haunted.
The doctor confirmed it was broken.

C1-4-0.title: Say, tell y el cambio de tiempo

items.a: He said that he was tired.
items.b: He told me that he was tired.
items.note: “Say” no lleva objeto personal; “tell” sí lo necesita.

items.a: He said me that he was tired.
items.b: He told me that he was tired.
items.note: La primera está mal: “said me” no existe.

items.a: She said the Earth is round.
items.b: She said the Earth was round.
items.note: Si algo sigue siendo cierto, no es obligatorio retroceder el tiempo.

C1-4-1.title: Del rumor a la pasiva impersonal

steps.label: Activa
steps.sentence: People **say** that the house is haunted.

steps.label: It + pasiva + that
steps.sentence: **It is said that** the house is haunted.

steps.label: Sujeto + pasiva + to
steps.sentence: The house **is said to be** haunted.

steps.label: Acción anterior
steps.sentence: He **is thought to have faked** the whole thing.
steps.change: to have + participio para algo anterior.

C1-4-1.title: ¿Qué infinitivo después de “is said / believed”?
C1-4-1.question: ¿Cuándo ocurre la acción comparada con el momento del reporte?

branches.example: He is believed to be innocent.
She is thought to be hiding abroad.
He is said to have left the country.
It is believed that he left the country.

C1-4-1.title: Qué tan segura es la información

items.example: He is alleged to have taken bribes.
The house is said to be haunted.
He is believed to be in Panama.
Ten people are reported to have been injured.
Smoking is known to cause cancer.

items.a: Frankly, she spoke to him.
items.b: She spoke to him frankly.
items.note: La primera: mi opinión sincera sobre el hecho. La segunda: ella habló con franqueza.

items.a: Honestly, I don’t know.
items.b: I answered honestly.
items.note: “Honestly,” al inicio comenta la frase; al final describe cómo respondí.

items.a: Clearly, he was tired.
items.b: He explained it clearly.
items.note: “Clearly,” = es evidente que; “clearly” al final = con claridad.

C1-5-0.title: ¿Qué adverbio de oración?
C1-5-0.question: ¿Qué actitud tienes ante lo que dices?

branches.example: Frankly, the ending was weak.

branches.if: Lo sabes por otros, no lo has comprobado
branches.example: Apparently, they’re filming a sequel.
Presumably, the budget was cut.
Luckily, nobody was hurt.
The plot was so confusing that nobody understood.

branches.if: Un sustantivo (con o sin adjetivo), singular contable
branches.example: It was such a long film that I fell asleep.
They were such good actors that we cried.
There were so many twists that I got lost.

steps.label: Dos ideas
steps.sentence: The film was boring. I left.

steps.label: Con so
steps.sentence: The film was **so boring that** I left.

steps.label: Con such
steps.sentence: It was **such a boring film that** I left.

steps.label: Inversión formal
steps.sentence: **So boring was the film that** I left.

items.a: It was such a long film.
items.b: It was so long film.
items.note: Con sustantivo usa “such a”, no “so”.

items.a: There was so much noise.
items.b: There was so many noise.
items.note: “Noise” es incontable: “so much”.

items.a: It was so long that I fell asleep.
items.b: It was so long I fell asleep.
items.note: Las dos son correctas: en el habla se puede omitir “that”.

steps.label: Dos ideas
steps.sentence: You practise more. You get better.

steps.label: Doble comparativo
steps.sentence: **The more** you practise, **the better** you get.

steps.label: Forma corta
steps.sentence: **The louder** the crowd, **the happier** the band.

steps.label: Expresión fija
steps.sentence: **The sooner, the better.**

items.a: The more you read, the more you learn.
items.b: More you read, more you learn.
items.note: “The” es obligatorio en las dos mitades.

items.a: The more you practise, the better you get.
items.b: How much you practise, better you get.
items.note: “Cuanto más” no se traduce con “how much”.

items.a: Concerts are getting more and more expensive.
items.b: Concerts are getting the more expensive.
items.note: Para un solo cambio continuo, usa “more and more”.

branches.if: Dos cosas cambian a la vez, una depende de la otra
branches.example: The older I get, the less I sleep.

branches.if: Una sola cosa cambia de forma continua
branches.example: It’s getting colder and colder.
The more, the merrier.
He’ll listen to the same album for weeks.

branches.if: Un hábito actual que te irrita
branches.example: She WILL leave the lights on!

branches.if: Una acción repetida en el pasado
branches.example: We would walk to the beach every morning.

branches.if: Un estado pasado (be, love, have, know)
branches.example: I used to love that band.
Water will boil at 100°C.

steps.label: Hábito presente
steps.sentence: My grandfather **will** sit on the porch for hours.

steps.label: Hábito pasado
steps.sentence: My grandfather **would** sit on the porch for hours.
steps.change: would = recuerdo de una acción repetida.

steps.label: Estado pasado
steps.sentence: My grandfather **used to** be a fisherman.

items.a: He’ll play music late.
items.b: He WILL play music late!
items.note: Sin énfasis, describe un hábito; con énfasis, muestra irritación.

items.a: I used to love that band.
items.b: I would love that band.
items.note: Con estados, “would” no expresa hábito pasado.

items.a: We would go to the river every Sunday.
items.b: We would go to the river once in 2005.
items.note: “Would” no sirve para una sola acción pasada.

C1-7-0.title: ¿Puedo omitir el pronombre?
C1-7-0.question: ¿Qué función cumple el pronombre en su cláusula?

branches.if: Es el objeto (después viene otro sujeto)
branches.example: The book (that) I read was brilliant.

branches.if: Es el sujeto (después viene el verbo)
branches.example: The man who called left a message.
The family whose house we bought moved away.
My aunt, who lives in Cali, called.

steps.label: Con pronombre objeto
steps.sentence: the house **that** we grew up in
steps.change: “we” es el sujeto de la cláusula.

steps.label: Omitido
steps.sentence: the house **we** grew up in

steps.label: Con pronombre sujeto
steps.sentence: the neighbour **who** moved in

steps.label: Omitido (incorrecto)
steps.sentence: the neighbour **moved in**
steps.change: ✗ Queda una frase distinta: el pronombre era obligatorio.

items.a: the house we grew up in
items.b: the house in which we grew up
items.note: La primera es natural al hablar; la segunda, en escritura cuidada.

items.a: the person I spoke to
items.b: the person to whom I spoke
items.note: “To whom” es muy formal; en conversación suena rígido.

items.a: the house in which we grew up
items.b: the house in that we grew up
items.note: Después de preposición nunca va “that”: usa “which” o “whom”.

branches.if: Una apariencia que puede ser real
branches.example: It looks as though the plan has changed.
He spends money as if he were a millionaire.

branches.if: Cómo se hace algo en realidad
branches.example: Do it the way your teacher explained.
She sings like an angel.

items.a: He looks as if he’s tired.
items.b: He looks as if he were a ghost.
items.note: La primera puede ser verdad; la segunda es claramente imaginaria.

items.a: She acts like a boss.
items.b: She acts as if she were the boss.
items.note: “Like” + sustantivo; “as if” + cláusula.

items.a: Do it as I told you.
items.b: Do it like I told you.
items.note: Las dos se entienden; “like” + cláusula es informal.

C1-7-1.title: Del hecho a la comparación imaginaria

steps.label: Realidad
steps.sentence: He isn’t a millionaire.

steps.label: Comparación irreal
steps.sentence: He spends money **as if he were** a millionaire.
steps.change: Pasado para marcar que no es real.

steps.label: Apariencia posible
steps.sentence: It **looks as though** it’s going to rain.

steps.label: Persona + cosa
steps.sentence: The clerk gave **me a refund**.
steps.change: Sin preposición; la cosa es la información nueva.

steps.label: Cosa + to + persona
steps.sentence: The clerk gave **a refund to me**.
steps.change: La persona queda al final y gana énfasis.

steps.label: Con pronombres
steps.sentence: Send **it to her**.
steps.change: Con dos pronombres, mejor la forma con “to”.

steps.label: Con for
steps.sentence: I bought **a gift for her**.

branches.if: give, send, show, offer, lend, tell
branches.use: sí: verbo + persona + cosa, o cosa + to + persona
branches.example: She showed me the photos. / She showed the photos to me.

branches.use: sí: verbo + persona + cosa, o cosa + for + persona
branches.example: He made me a cake. / He made a cake for me.
Explain the problem to me.

items.a: Explain the rule to me.
items.b: Explain me the rule.
items.note: Con “explain” la persona nunca va directamente después del verbo.

items.a: I bought a gift for her.
items.b: I bought a gift to her.
items.note: “Buy” usa “for”, no “to”.

items.a: Give it to me.
items.b: Give me it.
items.note: Con dos pronombres, la forma natural es “give it to me”.

steps.label: Indicativo (hecho)
steps.sentence: She **tries** a smaller size every time.

steps.label: Subjuntivo
steps.sentence: We recommend that she **try** a smaller size.
steps.change: Verbo base para todos los sujetos.

steps.label: Con be
steps.sentence: It is essential that he **be** refunded.

steps.label: Negativo
steps.sentence: We insist that he **not be** charged.

branches.example: We recommend that she apply early.
We recommend that she should apply early.
We recommend applying early.

branches.use: It is essential / vital that + verbo base
branches.example: It is vital that every form be signed.

items.a: I suggest that he call her.
items.b: I suggest that he calls her.
items.note: En el subjuntivo, sin -s.

items.a: I suggest that she take a break.
items.b: I suggest her to take a break.
items.note: “Suggest” no lleva objeto + infinitivo.

items.a: It’s vital that he be informed.
items.b: It’s vital that he is informed.
items.note: La segunda se oye en el habla británica, pero el subjuntivo formal usa “be”.

C1-9-0.title: ¿When/where o whenever/wherever?
C1-9-0.question: ¿Hablas de un momento o lugar concreto?

branches.example: They return to the beach where they were born.
They nest wherever the sand is warm.
Whenever it rains, the river rises.

branches.use: wherever / whenever (= no matter where / when)
branches.example: Wherever you go, you’ll find plastic.

items.a: Call me when you arrive.
items.b: Call me whenever you want.
items.note: La primera: en el momento de llegar. La segunda: a cualquier hora.

items.a: Sit where I can see you.
items.b: Sit wherever you like.
items.note: La primera: en un sitio concreto. La segunda: donde quieras.

items.a: Call me whenever you spot them.
items.b: Call me whenever you will spot them.
items.note: Después de -ever (y de when) no se usa “will”.

steps.label: Con no matter
steps.sentence: **No matter where** you look, there is plastic.

steps.label: Con wherever
steps.sentence: **Wherever** you look, there is plastic.

steps.label: Con every time
steps.sentence: **Every time** it rains, the river rises.

steps.label: Con whenever
steps.sentence: **Whenever** it rains, the river rises.

branches.example: Whoever litters here will be fined.
Take whatever you need.

branches.if: A una opción dentro de un grupo limitado
branches.example: Choose whichever seat is free.
Whatever happens, stay calm.

steps.label: Frase larga
steps.sentence: **Any person who** litters here will be fined.

steps.label: Con whoever
steps.sentence: **Whoever** litters here **will** be fined.
steps.change: La cláusula entera es el sujeto (singular).

steps.label: Frase larga
steps.sentence: You can take **anything that** you need.

steps.label: Con whatever
steps.sentence: You can take **whatever** you need.
steps.change: La cláusula entera es el objeto.

items.a: Whoever wants to help is welcome.
items.b: Whoever wants to help, he is welcome.
items.note: No repitas el sujeto con un pronombre.

items.a: Whoever wants to help is welcome.
items.b: Whoever want to help are welcome.
items.note: Con “whoever” como sujeto, el verbo va en singular.

items.a: Choose whichever you prefer: red or blue.
items.b: Choose whatever you prefer: red or blue.
items.note: Con pocas opciones concretas, “whichever” es más preciso.
